name: Dual Cable Front Raise
description: The dual cable front raise uses a cable behind the body from two low pulleys — one handle in each hand — raising both arms simultaneously to shoulder or eye level. The cables provide constant tension throughout the full range of motion, unlike dumbbells which unload near the top, making this variation superior for hypertrophy through the anterior deltoid and upper chest.

execution.starting_position: Stand between two low cable pulleys with one handle in each hand. Face away from the cable stack. Arms at sides, cables running from behind.
execution.setup_instructions: Set both pulleys to the lowest position. Adjust cable weights equally. Stand close to the cable stack initially to gauge tension.
steps: Step 1: Begin with arms at sides, cables taut running from behind.
Step 2: Raise both arms simultaneously forward and upward to shoulder height.
Step 3: Maintain slight elbow bend throughout — not fully locked, not deeply bent.
Step 4: Hold 1 second at shoulder height.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise. Inhale lowering.
common_mistakes: Raising above shoulder height — this recruits traps and reduces anterior delt emphasis
Using momentum from the torso — strict movement only
safety_considerations: Light loads recommended — anterior deltoid isolation exercises have high leverage disadvantage
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Arms at sides to shoulder height.
coaching_cues: Thumbs slightly up at the peak
No torso lean — strict upright posture
Lead with the pinkies as the arms rise
